blocks.title: Firewall Types exam shortcuts
items: Protect web app from SQLi/XSS → WAF
A WAF focuses on HTTP/HTTPS attacks.
Example: Malicious SQL input is blocked before reaching the application.
Firewall + AV + IDS/IPS in one → UTM
Example: A branch uses one security appliance.
NGFWs understand more than ports and IPs.
Example: Block an application regardless of port.
Rule based on HTTP/app content → LAYER 7
Example: Block a specific HTTP method.
blocks.example: Focus on the exact requirement in the scenario before choosing the control.

questions.q: A company wants to block SQL injection and XSS attempts before they reach its web application. Which firewall is best?
questions.explanation: A WAF specifically protects HTTP/HTTPS application traffic.

questions.q: A branch office wants one appliance that provides firewalling, antivirus, IDS/IPS, and web filtering. Which type best fits?
questions.explanation: UTM combines multiple security functions in one platform.

questions.q: A firewall must identify applications regardless of the TCP port they use and perform deep inspection. Which type is best?
questions.explanation: NGFWs provide application awareness and advanced inspection.

questions.q: A rule allows TCP 443 and blocks TCP 23 based only on ports and protocols. Which firewall layer is being used?
questions.explanation: Layer 4 filtering uses IP, port, and protocol information.

questions.q: A firewall blocks a specific HTTP method based on application content. Which layer is most relevant?
